newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ALOMAR HOMER LIFTS AMERICAN LEAGUE TO ALL-STAR WIN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ALOMAR HOMER LIFTS AMERICAN LEAGUE TO ALL-STAR WIN.

text.p: Hometown hero Sandy Alomar, Jr. of the Cleveland Indians thrilled fans at Jacobs Field Tuesday by smacking a two-run homer in the bottom of the seventh inning to lift the American League to a 3-1 victory over the National League in the 68th All-Star Game.
"It's an unbelievable feeling playing in front of a home town crowd and delivering like this. This is everybody's dream," said Alomar, the first Indian to win the All-Star Most Valuable Player Award.
Eight pitchers combined on a three-hitter for the American League stars, who ended a three-game All-Star losing streak to cut the National League's lead in the series to 40-27-1.

Alomar, the Cleveland catcher who carried a 30-game hitting streak into the Midsummer Classic, brought the crowd to its feet when he lined a 2-2 pitch from San Francisco Giants left-hander Shawn Estes into the bleachers in left-centre field.
"Sandy's having a magical year and he proved it tonight," said Alomar's teammate Jim Thome, the only other Cleveland player in the game.
Estes relieved Pedro Martinez of the Montreal Expos to start the seventh and retired Thome before walking Bernie Williams of the New York Yankees.

One out later, Alomar, who entered the game in the sixth, belted the third and final home run of the contest. He became the first Indian to homer in an All-Star Game since Rocky Colavito in 1959 and the first player to hit an All-Star homer in his home park since Hank Aaron in Atlanta in 1972.
AL and Yankees manager Joe Torre was delighted for Alomar.
"I played with his dad and can remember Sandy as a kid in the clubouse," Torre said. "Winning the World Series last year and now the All-Star game is a dream."
Kansas City Royals rookie Jose Rosado got the win, despite allowing a solo homer to Atlanta Braves catcher Javy Lopez that tied the game at 1-1 in the top of the seventh.
Randy Myers of the Baltimore Orioles struck out two in a perfect eighth and Mariano Rivera of the Yankees retired all three batters he faced in the ninth to pick up the save.

The American League broke a 15-inning All-Star scoreless drought when Edgar Martinez of the Seattle Mariners led off the second by lining a 2-2 pitch from Atlanta's Greg Maddux over the left-field wall for a 1-0 lead.
"It was very satisfying to hit a home run off Maddux, who is one of the best pitchers in baseball," Martinez said.

Martinez's blast was just the second homer by a designated hitter in an All-Star Game, joining Florida's Jeff Conine, who did it in 1995. The DH has been used in All-Star Games at AL parks since 1989.

The NL managed just one hit through the first six innings -- a single by Jeff Blauser of the Braves in the third -- before Lopez took a low 2-2 pitch from Rosado and banged it high off the left-field foul pole. He was the 11th player to homer in his first All-Star at-bat.
Rosado allowed a single to Moises Alou of the Marlins and a walk to Ray Lankford of the St. Louis Cardinals, but escaped further damage by striking out St. Louis' Royce Clayton.
Randy Johnson of Seattle was dominant in his second All-Star start, pitching two hitless innings with strikeouts of Craig Biggio of Houston and Barry Bonds of San Francisco in the first.
The only batter to reach base against Johnson was Larry Walker of Colorado, who drew a comical walk with two outs in the second.
Walker, criticised for avoiding a meeting with Johnson during an interleague game last month, watched as the first pitch sailed far over his head.
Walker then put his batting helmet on backwards and turned around and batted right-handed for the next pitch -- a strike.
The scene had players and coaches on both benches, and Johnson, convulsed with laughter. Walker and Johnson had been teammates in the Montreal organisation years earlier.
Walker returned to his regular batting stance and Johnson followed with three straight balls to complete the walk.
Maddux allowed just one run on the homer to Martinez and two hits in two innings.
The National League threatened in the fourth when David Cone of the New York Yankees, who followed Toronto's Roger Clemens to the mound, walked Bonds and Mike Piazza of the Los Angeles Dodgers.
But Piazza was caught in a rundown when catcher Ivan Rodriguez of the Texas Rangers scooped up a pitch in the dirt and threw to second. With Bonds at third, Walker grounded out to end the threat.
Cal Ripken of the Orioles, making his 15th All-Star appearance, had four assists in five innings at third base. He was lifted for a pinch-runner after singling in the bottom of the fifth.
